title: Universe compatibility of finite-cone categorical-pattern models
statement:
Fix nested Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P=(B,S,\{p_a:K_a^{\triangleleft}\to B\}_{a\in A})$ be a $\mathcal U$-small categorical pattern as in [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], with all $2$-simplices of $B$ included in the scaling. Assume that every $K_a$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices; empty $K_a$ are allowed. Use marked simplicial sets, their markings $K^\flat$ and $K^\sharp$, and monomorphisms from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and the pattern model structures $\mathsf M_P(\mathcal U)$ and $\mathsf M_P(\mathcal U')$ from [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus], formed with the identical fixed pattern $P$.

The following maps form a common $\mathcal U$-small generating set of cofibrations in both model structures: $(\partial\Delta^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$, for every $n\geq0$ and simplex $\Delta^n\to B$, and $(\Delta^1)^\flat\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, for every edge of $S$. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of the proper faces of the standard simplex. A generating set $I$ means that the cofibrations are exactly the retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of maps of $I$, with coproducts and transfinite sequences small in the universe of that model structure. A $\mathcal U$-small marked object is fibrant in one model structure if and only if it is fibrant in the other. A map between $\mathcal U$-small marked objects is a weak equivalence in one model structure if and only if it is a weak equivalence in the other. There are functorial fibrant replacements $X\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{\mathcal U}X$ and $X'\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{\mathcal U'}X'$ and a natural isomorphism $\iota R_{\mathcal U}\cong R_{\mathcal U'}\iota$, compatible with these replacement maps, where $\iota$ is the inclusion of the smaller marked objects into the larger ones. In particular, $R_{\mathcal U}X$ is $\mathcal U$-small for every $\mathcal U$-small $X$.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definition B.1.1 (seven pattern-anodyne generator types), Proposition B.1.6 (fibrancy), Lemma B.2.4 (homotopy-inverse criterion), and proof of Theorem B.0.20 (small-object fibrant replacement), printed pp.1470-1471,1483,1485-1487. Universe compatibility is the finite-generator small-object consequence expanded in report.md; not a separately numbered theorem. Marked cofibration generators also occur in the proof of Proposition B.1.9, printed p.1476. No Stacks tag states this result.
